data.content: , provided "an argument that could be made" with respect to the legal status of Taiwan
I do not think there is any purpose in my letter of today
of introducing an argument in it as to the legal situation of Formosa. You might, however, think over an argument that could be made; namely, that Formosa and the Pescadores are still in
's jurisdiction. The Japanese acquired them from China in 1895. In subsequent years, we frequently ratified the status quo of their possessions.

The Cairo Declaration and the Potsdam surrender were executive acts which were never matters of treaties ratified by the Senate. Such a ratification would only come up in a treaty with Japan, and MacArthur might collaterally hold them pending a treaty.
